claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films or patterned nanoribbons have high residual strain and an inhomogeneous defect distribution.
Residual strain and an inhomogeneous defect distribution produce irregular magnetic domain structures in the as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi material.
Rapid post-deposition thermal annealing will partially relax residual strain in nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films.
Rapid thermal annealing will decrease defects that act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Heat treatment will produce a more magnetically uniform domain structure.
Reduced strain and defect pinning will facilitate magnetic-domain-wall motion during field cycling.
Easier domain-wall motion will narrow magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation and reduced pinning will increase the magnitude and reversibility of the magnetic entropy change under low applied fields.
A short, moderate-temperature anneal below the phase-transformation threshold can relax strain without promoting phase segregation.
Excessive annealing may cause phase separation or over-relaxation and degrade magnetocaloric performance.
The proposed effect applies under low magnetic fields, exemplified as fields below 1 T, near the intrinsic magnetic transition.
Heat-transfer rate in the nanoscale geometry limits the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Continuous films and lithographically patterned nanoribbons may respond differently to annealing.
The optimal annealing temperature and duration for achieving strain relaxation without unwanted phase changes are not established.

contradictions.description: Performance degradation after excessive annealing is presented as an anticipated out-of-boundary outcome, but the falsification rule also treats degradation from over-annealing as falsifying the bounded hypothesis. An outcome explicitly expected outside the permitted annealing window cannot by itself falsify the claim about controlled moderate annealing.
